sec: Bone types and trabecular bone assessment · p863

items.q: The skeletal system receives what share of total cardiac output?
items.exp: The skeletal system is highly vascular — 10% of total cardiac output. (Book p863)

items.q: Match cortical vs trabecular bone — 1) Cortical contribution  2) Trabecular contribution  3) Cortical unit  4) Trabecular unit … A) Trabeculae  B) 20%  C) 80%  D) Osteon
items.exp: Cortical bone = 80% of mass, osteon unit; trabecular = 20%, trabeculae. (Book p863)

items.q: Cortical bone is seen in ___ and trabecular bone in ___.
opts: Diaphysis of long bone; epiphysis and vertebrae
items.exp: Cortical in diaphysis of long bones; trabecular in epiphysis and vertebrae. (Book p863)

items.q: ‘The Haversian system is present in cortical bone but absent in trabecular bone.’
Match hormone action on bone type — 1) Cortical bone  2) Trabecular bone … A) Steroid hormones  B) PTH and thyroid
items.exp: PTH and thyroid act on cortical bone; steroid hormones on trabecular bone. (Book p863)

items.q: Trabecular bone has a HIGH remodelling rate because of:
items.exp: High remodelling/bone turnover d/t ↑ surface area to mass ratio; also high metabolic activity and porosity. (Book p863)

items.q: Osteoporosis is evaluated on trabecular bone using:
opts: Bone mineral density (BMD) and trabecular bone score (TBS)
items.exp: BMD plus the newer trabecular bone score (TBS). (Book p863)

items.q: Two patients have near-identical BMD (L1–L4 ≈ 0.99) but TBS 1.432 vs 1.124. The patient with TBS 1.124 has:
opts: Degraded micro-architecture → osteoporosis despite similar BMD
items.exp: Normal TBS (1.432) = good micro-architecture; low TBS (1.124) = degraded micro-architecture → osteoporosis. (Book p863)
